title: Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom
summary: Anansi tries to hide a magical pot of wisdom, but a clever child offers help.
coverScene: A clever spider sits near a clay pot in a green forest.

sentences.text: Long ago, before many towns were built, the world was a quiet and secluded place where people lived in small groups and shared food every single day.
Anansi was a man who wanted to be wiser than anyone else, spending his time scheming about ways to gain ultimate power over his peers.
When the sky god offered him a large clay vessel containing all the knowledge of the world, Anansi felt an immense surge of pride.
He believed that if he held every piece of information, he would instantly become the most important person alive.
He thought that his grand plan would work without any trouble at all, failing to foresee the heavy burden of his own ambition.
The pot was heavy and brimming with ancient wisdom that had accumulated since the dawn of creation.
Anansi carried this precious container everywhere he went, guarding it with fierce and obsessive suspicion.
He did not want anyone else to look inside the pot, terrified that a single secret might slip away into the hands of a stranger.
Every time someone asked him about the mysterious vessel, he turned his back and walked away in silence.
He wanted to keep all the secrets hidden from public view, entirely convinced that true wisdom should be locked away.
The tree was tall and green, standing proudly in the middle of a dense and quiet forest.
Anansi decided that this remote location would serve as the ideal hiding place for his stolen universe of facts.
To bring the heavy pot up the tree, he tied a long and durable string around its ceramic neck.
Climbing that trunk with the awkward load proved to be the hardest physical challenge he had ever faced.
He tried to haul the container upward, but the sheer weight dragged against his chest with relentless force.
Carrying the pot directly in front of his stomach made every upward movement agonizingly difficult and clumsy.
His protruding stomach pushed awkwardly against the round surface, causing him to lose his balance on the rough bark.
He could not reach the higher branches because the large pot completely blocked his forward vision and his path.
His young child, who stood firmly on the soil below, watched him struggle with this strange and misguided task.
The boy felt deeply worried as he observed his father fighting against a problem of his own making.
The boy was young, but his mind was sharp and he understood the mechanical dilemma right away.
He spoke to his father in a clear, calm, and remarkably helpful voice that cut through the rustling leaves.
He asked why his father did not simply tie the heavy pot to his back instead of holding it in front.
Anansi heard the words and instantly knew that they made complete logical sense.
He felt a sudden wave of foolishness wash over him because he had completely failed to see that obvious solution.
Anansi realized with a shock that the child was entirely right, which wounded his profound pride.
He felt deeply surprised and deeply unsettled because he had foolishly thought he already knew everything worth knowing.
In his sudden anger and shock, his grip loosened and he accidentally dropped the pot down toward the earth.
The fragile ceramic vessel plummeted through the branches and shattered into a million small pieces upon the hard ground.
All the accumulated knowledge flew out like a sudden gale into the wind and spread across the whole world.
Anansi sat down heavily on a cold stone and watched the wind carry the precious secrets far away.
He realized with a heavy heart that some things simply cannot belong to just one single person.
The sky god looked down slowly from the distant clouds, watching the man with a silent, knowing gaze.
Life would go on as before, but the world had fundamentally changed in a single unforgettable moment.
Everyone in the wide world now shared a portion of the knowledge that had once been locked inside the pot.
He walked around the base of the great tree for many long hours as the afternoon sun began to dip.
He thought deeply about the shattered pot and the vast information that had slipped through his clumsy fingers.
He knew that the world was large and full of hidden places, tempting him to search for the scattered pieces.
He looked under every green plant and behind every grey rock, hoping to reclaim what he had lost.
The wind blew softly through the tall green tree while the boy watched his father search the dirt.
The sun went down slowly behind the distant hills, painting the horizon in shades of amber and violet.
Night came quickly over the land, bringing a blanket of deep silence and glittering stars.
Anansi sat on his stone and rested his tired hands, finally accepting the limits of his own mind.
The young child sat quietly beside his father and spoke gentle words of comfort into the evening air.
They stayed together under the boughs until the pale morning light finally appeared over the horizon.
Many years passed after that strange and humbling event, changing the daily lives of everyone in the land.
People grew older and eagerly taught their children many useful things, passing wisdom from hand to hand.
Schools eventually opened in every town across the country, welcoming eager pupils into bright classrooms.
Teachers shared books and information with happy students who absorbed new words every single day.
The world transformed completely because knowledge was finally free and accessible for all people.
Anansi often remembered the big pot and the green tree when he walked through the village.
He smiled gently whenever he saw local children reading books together in the cool shade of the courtyard.
His family lived happily through all the changing seasons, finding joy in simple and shared conversations.
The sky god remained high above the clouds, watching over a wiser and more united human race.
No one ever tried to hoard the world information again, ensuring that stories would be told for generations.
